intent: Inline section message (callout) with a colored edge bar: contextual info, warnings, errors, successes, or discovery announcements embedded in page flow. For full-width page-level announcements use the .banner subcomponent; for floating toast notifications use .flag.

structure.description: Row of action links after the body text.

a11yNotes: Tone is conveyed by color only — make the text itself state the severity (the title usually does). Messages inserted dynamically should get role="status" (or role="alert" for errors) so they are announced.
examples:
Trial ending

Your trial expires in 3 days.

Upgrade

subcomponents.intent: Full-width single-line page banner (maintenance notices, read-only mode, outages). Sits above or below the navbar spanning the viewport; content is centered and links inherit the bold text color.
subcomponents.a11yNotes: Banners on bold backgrounds keep sufficient contrast via on-bold tokens; .banner-inverse uses the tooltip surface pair (events, launches) instead. If a banner appears dynamically (e.g. connection lost) give it role="status" / role="alert".
examples: Lozenge Summit 2026 — tickets are live. Register now

subcomponents.intent: Floating toast notification (bottom-left in Jira): icon, content block (title/description/actions), and a dismiss button. Add .flag-fixed to pin it to the viewport; bold tone variants recolor the whole flag for success/error toasts. It is a glass surface.

structure.description: The flexible middle block (flex:1, min-width:0) holding .flag-title, optional .flag-description, and optional .flag-actions.
Optional leading icon block (e.g. an .issue-type square), flex-shrink:0.

allowedIn: directly under <body> (with .flag-fixed), or a toast stack container

subcomponents.a11yNotes: Toasts appear asynchronously: give the flag (or its container) role="status", or role="alert" for error flags, so screen readers announce it. .flag-dismiss must carry aria-label (its content is just ×). The flag is a glass surface — never nest another glass surface (dropdown-menu, modal, navbar, another flag) inside it, and never mount a flag inside one; glass-on-glass compounds blur and voids the contrast guarantees.
